body.text: In what analysts are calling less a "battle" and more a "structured humiliation," the Royal Air Force 1 Commando's Scrim Team dismantled USAR 75th Ranger Regiment's Scrim Team in a scoreline that has left mathematicians questioning whether the number 101 was even necessary.

Witnesses on the ground described the engagement as "not so much a scrim as a public service announcement." One anonymous 75th Ranger operative was seen staring blankly into the middle distance, muttering "we had a plan" before being gently escorted away by teammates.

This reporter was present, inebriated, and, with all due modesty, seemed to think the Rangers simply had no answer for his continued flanking of their team. Repeated flanking. Almost suspiciously effective flanking.
RAF 1 Commando's commanding officer offered a brief statement: "We'd like to thank the Rangers for showing up. Genuinely, thank you. It meant a lot to us."
The 75th Ranger Regiment have not yet commented, because we haven't asked them.
Fish News will continue to monitor the situation, though frankly there isn't much left to monitor.
